subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): skip malformed legacy import-run files in doctor

question: After valid records migrate, should malformed or schema-invalid legacy import-run files remain in place with repeated warnings, or be moved to an explicit rejected/quarantine artifact?
rationale: Both choices affect persisted legacy user data and subsequent doctor runs; source inspection cannot determine the intended migration policy without owner intent.

options.title: Retain with warning
options.body: Leave rejected files untouched so doctor never renames or discards data it could not validate, accepting repeated warnings until the user acts.

options.title: Quarantine rejected files
options.body: Move rejected files to an explicitly named quarantine artifact so future doctor runs are clean, with additional migration and recovery semantics to define and test.

recommendation.title: Retain with warning
recommendation.body: Leave rejected files untouched so doctor never renames or discards data it could not validate, accepting repeated warnings until the user acts.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite migration and its legacy archive policy originated in their merged Memory Wiki refactor.
